name: Overhead press
pattern: Vertical push: the weight goes from the shoulders to straight arms overhead while the shoulder blades rotate up.
setup: Stand with feet hip width, bar on the front of your shoulders.
Hands just outside the shoulders, wrists stacked over the elbows, forearms vertical.
Squeeze glutes and brace, ribs down: no big lean back.

steps.text: Start with the bar at your collarbones, elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Move your head back a little and press the bar straight up past your face.
Finish with arms straight, bar over your mid-foot, head through between the arms.
Bring the bar back down the same line to the collarbones.

cues.cue: Ribs down, glutes tight: stand tall, do not lean back.
cues.why: Standing presses need trunk stiffness; the spine moves about 12-15° during the press and more without bracing.

cues.cue: Bar in front of your face, finish over the back of your head.
cues.why: Pressing in front avoids the end-range externally rotated position linked to shoulder instability.

cues.cue: Let them rotate up; at lockout reach tall.
cues.why: At full arm elevation the shoulder blade rotates up about 50° and tilts back; that clears room for the rotator cuff.

cues.cue: Elbows a little in front of the bar, forearms vertical.
cues.why: Vertical forearms push the load straight up through the arm.

cues.cue: Bar low in the palm, wrists only slightly bent.
cues.why: Bent-back wrists move the bar behind the forearm and strain the wrist.

breathing: Breathe in and brace at the shoulders, breathe out after lockout.

tempo.note: Press in about 1 s, lower in 2 s.

mistakes.name: Leaning back
mistakes.looks: The lower back arches and the chest points up as you press.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes, ribs down; use less weight.
mistakes.why: It turns the press into an incline press and loads the lower back.

mistakes.name: Bar stays in front
mistakes.looks: At the top the bar is in front of the head, arms angled forward.
mistakes.fix: Push your head through once the bar passes your forehead.
mistakes.why: The load sits forward of the shoulder and the arms never reach full elevation.

mistakes.name: Elbows flare behind the bar
mistakes.looks: Elbows point straight out to the sides at the start, bar drifts forward.
mistakes.fix: Bring elbows slightly forward, forearms vertical.
mistakes.why: It puts the shoulder near the high-five position with the load behind it.

mistakes.name: Wrists bent back
mistakes.looks: Knuckles point back, bar sits on the fingers.
mistakes.fix: Bar low in the palm over the forearm.
mistakes.why: The bar's weight bends the wrist instead of stacking on the forearm.

safety: Behind-the-neck pressing needs full shoulder external rotation; press in front if you lack it.
Shoulder pain overhead: use a landmine press or a neutral-grip dumbbell press.
Lower-back pain: sit with back support or kneel.

variants.change: Seated: less trunk demand and more 1RM; deltoid activity a bit lower than standing.
Dumbbells: deltoid activity about 7-15% higher than barbell but about 7% less weight.
Behind the neck: needs full external rotation and a straight upper back.
Palms facing each other, elbows forward: often easier on the shoulder.
Kneeling: the trunk has to resist leaning back.
Sitting on the floor legs straight: no leg or back help, strict torso.
Kettlebell bottom up: grip and rotator cuff work much harder; light weight.
One side: resist leaning to the side.
Curl first, then press from the shoulder.

subtypes.name: Arnold press
subtypes.change: Start with palms facing you in front of the shoulders, open the elbows to the sides and turn the palms forward as you press.

subtypes.name: Landmine press
subtypes.change: One end of a bar in the floor; press the other end up and forward on a diagonal, often half-kneeling. Arm finishes about 120-135° raised, so it is kinder to stiff shoulders.

subtypes.name: Pike push-up
subtypes.change: Hands on the floor, hips high in an upside-down V, lower the top of your head toward the floor in front of the hands.

subtypes.name: Handstand and handstand push-up
subtypes.change: Upside down on your hands, body in one line, usually against a wall. Push tall through the shoulders; balance is kept mostly at the wrists. Handstand push-ups lower the head to the floor or between benches.

subtypes.name: Seated press
subtypes.change: Sitting with back support, hips and knees about 90°: same arm keyframes as the standing press.

subtypes.name: Dumbbell press
subtypes.change: Dumbbells start at ear height, elbows about 30° in front of the body line; press up and slightly in. Same arm keyframes.

subtypes.name: Cuban press
subtypes.change: Upright row to elbow height, rotate the forearms up to vertical, then press: light weight, a rotator cuff drill.

motion.basis: Scapular upward rotation at full elevation (about 46-50°, posterior tilt about 30°, glenohumeral to scapular ratio 1.7-2:1) from mcclure2001 and ludewig2009, scaled to arm angle at each keyframe. Spine movement of 12-15° from mckean2015. Rack, mid-press and lockout shoulder and elbow angles, shoulder rotation (forearm vertical at the rack gives about 60° external rotation) and the inverted subtypes are estimates from the bar path; no study measured them directly. Handstand balance mostly at the wrists from mcdonald2025.
